transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-21
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Carlos (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Elena (CTO, MeridianRx), Markus (SRE), Aisha (ML Eng)

Summary:
Quick sync on week 3 POC results — focus on throughput and horizon latency vs their incumbent provider (IncumbentCloud). Went over anomalous tail latency, routing fallbacks, quantization impact and next steps to run an on-prem throughput run. Agreed to share raw logs and a cost spreadsheet.

Topics covered:
- P50/P95/P99 latency comparison vs incumbent baseline
- Throughput scaling at 100/500/1k concurrent requests
- Batching, KV cache, and quantization tradeoffs
- Routing and fallback policy causing 200ms spikes in Europe region
- Security/compliance ask re: audit logs and KMS

Transcript:
[00:00] Carlos (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um — I know we're on a tight schedule today so we'll go straight into the numbers. Priya will walk through the lab results first.
[00:36] Priya (Redwood SE): Yeah hi, thanks. So quick recap, this week we ran three blocks: single-node hosted run, multi-node dedicated sim, and an on-prem replicate using your staging hardware image. The big wins are on throughput with continuous batching, but we saw a tail outlier at P99 around 380–420 ms under the dedicated pool for longer sequences.
[01:10] Aisha (MeridianRx): Sorry just to clarify, is that with quantize turned on? Our baseline with the incumbent had quantize but a different Q8 profile, might be why numbers differ.
[01:24] Priya: Good call — the run I showed uses Redwood quantization profile 'q8-int' (auto-tuned). For transparency we also did a float16 run; p50 is slightly better with q8 but p99 is noisier when KV cache misses happen.
[01:46] Markus: We're seeing similar with our internal tests. The incumbent's p99 is quoted lower but that's because they offload to a smaller seq len and they warm caches differently. Can you share the exact seed prompts and cache warmup?
[02:05] Priya: Yes, we'll attach the prompt set and the cache prefill script. There may be a mismatch — we prefilled to five prefixes, but their baseline used a longer prefix distribution.
[02:30] Carlos: Quick commercial check — when you compare cost, what's the biggest driver? Is it GPU sku or token count from extra retries on tail?
[02:41] Elena: For us it's both. Cost matters but if latency spikes cause front-end errors, that's worse. Our success metric is 95% of requests under 200ms at 500 rps.
[02:58] Priya: Right. For the 500 rps steady load we achieved p50=72ms p95=168ms p99=395ms on Redwood Dedicated with batching=32 and seq_len=512. IncumbentCloud numbers that you provided were p50=80ms p95=150ms p99=310ms — so our p95 is comparable, p99 is higher in that run.
[03:27] Aisha: Huh okay. Did the incumbent run include prefix caching? I suspect their workload is more optimized for the exact prompts we use in prod.
[03:40] Priya: Their cache hit pattern looked like it favored shorter prefixes. We suspect our prefill pattern needs to mimic prod more closely.
[03:52] Markus: Another data point — last Tuesday we saw routing flips between eu-west and us-east causing a 200–400 ms jump for a subset of requests. Any idea why Redwood routing would do that?
[04:06] Priya: That's likely the smart routing fallback kicking in during capacity pressure — we had a simulated cap breach in one of the dedicated nodes and the routing policy moved to a compatible variant in us-east. We can tighten thresholds or enable region pinning for your tenant.
[04:22] Carlos: Region pinning is an option, but might cost more. We can show cost delta.
[04:28] Elena: We'll need the SLA implications documented. Also, SOC2 and audit logs — are those already in the security deck you shared?
[04:37] Carlos: Yes, we sent a security pack last week but we'll re-share the on-prem KMS/HSM notes. For SOC2 compliance, Redwood Private package supports required audits.
[04:50] Priya: Back to performance — we did an experiment with smaller batching (batching=8) which drops p99 to ~330ms but increases GPU utilization and thus cost per token. There's a clear tradeoff surface.
[05:06] Aisha: Can you quantify cost delta for that config? We need numbers to trade off latency vs unit-cost for our product manager.
[05:15] Carlos: Yep that's on the action list — I'll produce a spreadsheet comparing batching 8/16/32 and quantize profiles with cost-per-1M tokens.
[05:25] Elena: Also, can we run a 6-hour soak at 1k rps with the exact header shapes we get from prod? The incumbent offered us that and it helped them tune better.
[05:36] Priya: We can — on dedicated it's straightforward; for on-prem we'll need your runbook and access to the staging runner. Markus, can you share the scripts?
[05:44] Markus: I'll drop the load generator and the header sample in the shared folder after this call.
[05:51] Priya: Great. One weirdness to call out — in the hosted run we saw sporadic tokenization differences that made one prompt longer and bumped seq_len unexpectedly. The tokenizer mapping for Lama3-ish models sometimes spits out different subwords. That affected our batching harmony.
[06:12] Aisha: Wait, we're using Lama3-8b-fp16 variant? Our earlier notes say Lama3-13b. Could mismatch be the root cause?
[06:22] Priya: Yeah there was a model mapping mixup in the first run — we corrected it mid-week but the initial numbers included that noise. We'll tag which run used which model.
[06:33] Carlos: So plan of record — replicate incumbent's prefix distribution, run extended soak at 1k rps, tighten routing to avoid eu-west fallback, and share cost sheet.
[06:43] Elena: Sounds good. Quick question on encryption in transit for on-prem; we need HSM integration for keys, is that available?
[06:52] Carlos: Yes, Redwood Private can integrate with your HSM/KMS. We'll include the integration doc and a contact for our security engineer.
[07:02] Markus: On the failover front — if routing moves requests to a different model variant, do you preserve KV cache or is that a cold start?
[07:12] Priya: It's a cold start for the model variant unless the variants are binary-compatible and we can share the KV cache. We have a cache warming flow though to avoid a big cold-penalty in production traffic.
[07:25] Aisha: Could that explain the 200ms spikes? A cold switch would add token latency.
[07:31] Priya: Yes, that aligns.
[07:36] Carlos: Ok let's move to the anomalous week-over-week regressed run you flagged, Priya — what did we change between the two runs?
[07:45] Priya: We changed the quant profile and bumped the batch size. The regression seems correlated with a third-party library update in the serving runtime that changed micro-batching ordering. It only showed up on the dedicated multi-node sim.
[08:02] Elena: Is that a Redwood runtime change? We need a changelog for internal compliance.
[08:08] Priya: Yes, that was an internal optimization. We'll provide the changelog entry and a patch note.
[08:15] Carlos: Anything else on security or procurement?
[08:19] Elena: Procurement wants an escrow for logs and a list of sub-processors. Also, do you provide per-route tracing to tie latency to token boundaries?
[08:29] Priya: We have per-request traces and token-level logs in the Console. For Private installs we can enable retention windows and forward to your SIEM.
[08:39] Markus: Great. From an ops perspective we need the load generator config (we'll paste it) and if Redwood can run the 6-hour soak with our headers that would be ideal.
[08:49] Priya: We'll stand that up. One question — do you want us to run with region pinning on the soak or let smart routing do PR spread?
[08:57] Elena: Let's pin to eu-west for the soak to avoid cross-region noise. We want to isolate infra variability first.
[09:04] Carlos: Perfect. Next steps recap: Priya runs extended soak pinned to eu-west on dedicated infra, Markus shares load generator, Carlos sends cost/latency sheet, and Priya shares raw logs and prompt set.
[09:18] Aisha: Can you also include the batching heatmap you mentioned? That was useful in the deck.
[09:24] Priya: Yep will include heatmap and the cache prefill script.
[09:29] Elena: If the soak shows improved p99 we can discuss moving to a month-long pilot and talk about Dedicated reserved slots.
[09:37] Carlos: Sounds like a plan. Any final questions?
[09:42] Markus: One small thing — can you include the exact kernel selection details? We want to ensure it's reproducible for on-prem.
[09:50] Priya: We'll add the kernel and compilation flags used in the run artifacts.
[09:55] Carlos: Great. I'll follow up with dates. Thanks everyone.
[10:00] Elena: Thanks all.

End of transcript.

Notes about transcript quality: automated transcription caught most names but sometimes labeled 'Priya' as 'Priyia' in the raw, and 'Llama' came out as 'Lama' in a couple places. Some timestamps are approximate.

Attachments referenced: shared/meridianrx/prompt_set_v3.txt, shared/meridianrx/cache_prefill.sh, shared/meridianrx/loadgen_config.json, security/redwood_private_kms.pdf, cost-sheets/batching-latency-costs.csv

Meeting close: agreed next sync after soak results, tentative 2026-05-29 for quick readout.
